mainEntity.name: What does MVP1 Ventures actually do?

acceptedAnswer.text: We scale software companies that already have customers, and we automate the businesses that run on software without selling it. Either way, we stay accountable for what the work is supposed to achieve commercially, not just for shipping it.

mainEntity.name: Which track am I, software company or SMB?

acceptedAnswer.text: Software companies need a product engineered to scale and transformed with AI. SMBs need the work itself automated. If you sell software as your product, you're the software company track. If software is how your business runs but not what you sell, you're the SMB track.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the code and IP after the engagement?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do. Code, IP and assets are yours. We build it that way because owned assets don't just run cleaner, they lift your company's valuation, and that only works if you actually hold the assets.

mainEntity.name: Is MVP1 ISO 27001 certified?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Our Information Security Management System is certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, covering the design, development, deployment, maintenance and support of custom software, SaaS, marketplace platforms, mobile applications and AI-driven automation. Certificate AMER501362.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between MVP1 and BlackVault?

acceptedAnswer.text: BlackVault is our venture for clients who cannot send data to a US-domiciled AI platform, government, healthcare and financial services. It's private, sovereign AI infrastructure that runs inside the client's own environment: the data never leaves, every action is logged, and the capability is owned rather than rented. MVP1 serves founders and operating businesses with product engineering and AI agents. Different buyer, different delivery model.

mainEntity.name: Is this a chatbot, or does MVP1 build actual AI agents?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not a chatbot bolted onto a broken process. We redesign the work itself, then build agents that carry it end-to-end, with your people reviewing, approving, and staying in control.

mainEntity.name: Where does a human fit in if agents are doing the work?

acceptedAnswer.text: At sign-off. Your team reviews and approves what the agent has prepared. Decisions stay accountable, with a full audit trail.

mainEntity.name: What parts of my business can actually be automated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Onboarding and intake, back-office operations like data entry and reconciliation, compliance evidence and reporting, customer support triage, and sales pipeline research and follow-up are the places we see the most hours recovered first. We map your specific process before recommending anything.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my platform needs stabilising?

acceptedAnswer.text: Performance drops or outages as usage grows, every new feature breaks two old ones, security and compliance gaps you can't fully see, a codebase only one person understands (or no one does), and an MVP that got you to customers but can't get you to scale, those are the five signs.

mainEntity.name: Will stabilising disrupt my current customers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The point is to stabilise the platform while it keeps running and serving customers, not to take it offline to fix it.

mainEntity.name: I built my product with ChatGPT, Claude, Lovable or Replit. Is that a problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on its own, it's a fast way to validate an idea. The problem shows up at deployment, security and scale, since AI-generated code is rarely production-hardened by default. We audit it, harden what needs hardening, and get it to a state that can carry real users.

mainEntity.name: What counts as "production-grade" engineering?

acceptedAnswer.text: Architecture, security, and delivery discipline built for real load, not a demo that works until real customers show up. Every build carries full ownership: you hold the code and the IP from day one.

mainEntity.name: I only have an idea, not a product yet. Is that too early for MVP1?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for this track. Our Accelerate Program de-risks the idea first, so when you do build, you build the right thing instead of guessing.

Real, verifiable outcomes on the Our Work page include an e-signature platform's monthly recurring revenue turnaround after re-engineering, a transport and logistics platform scaling from 3 to 12 centres, and an NDIS onboarding process cut from 7 to 8 hours down to under 90 minutes.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the assessment says no?

acceptedAnswer.text: You exit informed, with capital preserved and a documented rationale you can show a board or a co-founder. We are paid for the rigour of the assessment, not for a particular answer. A no delivered during the assessment is a better outcome than the same conclusion reached after a six-figure build.

mainEntity.name: How is the assessment priced?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engagement is scoped first and priced second. You get a fixed price for a fixed scope, confirmed in writing before you commit — not a rate card, and not an hourly rate that turns into a blank cheque. No additional charges are required to complete the agreed scope. Book a fit call and we will scope it and quote it. For context, a first build that fails commercially typically costs a six-figure sum, and the founder time that went with it.

mainEntity.name: What does the engagement ask of me?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four live working sessions plus a structured intake pack. We agree the schedule with you when we scope the engagement, and your lead keeps you posted on progress and deliverables throughout. Expect roughly six to eight hours of your own time. You bring domain expertise, industry knowledge and competitor awareness; we do the modelling, research and production between sessions.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the deliverables and the IP?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do, on payment. The assessment outputs and all venture-specific material are yours. The licence back to us covers our own methodologies and frameworks only, and expressly excludes your confidential information, venture concept, business model, customer insight, financial assumptions and commercial analysis. Any public reference to you or your venture requires your prior written approval.

mainEntity.name: Is the commercial model something I can actually use?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. It is a live Excel model, not a PDF. A distinct assumptions register drives every downstream calculation, scenarios switch from a single cell, and the logic is transparent enough to defend line by line in a board meeting. It is built so you understand the drivers of your own business, not to impress you. Projections are indicative and are not financial advice.

mainEntity.name: Can you build the platform afterwards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but there is no obligation. Design, development, launch and ongoing support are separate engagements, quoted against a completed scope rather than a guess. The handover package is deliberately built so any competent development team can build from it — you are never dependent on the firm that holds the documentation.

mainEntity.name: Do I need this if I already have a prototype?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes. A working prototype proves the software can be built; it does not prove anyone will pay for it, or that the unit economics survive contact with the market. Teams arriving with a vibe-coded build from ChatGPT, Claude, Lovable, Manus or Replit are a common case — the code exists, the commercial case has never been tested. The assessment tests the business, not the build.

mainEntity.name: What happens if scope changes mid-engagement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing happens without your written approval and an updated proposal. Scope questions are raised inside 48 hours, and no work proceeds past a quality gate without sign-off. That governance is as much the product as the deliverables are.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The handover pack is deliberately vendor-neutral — specifications, assets, native Figma files and component documentation any competent development team can build from. We earn the build engagement on the quality of the definition work, not by holding your assets.

mainEntity.name: What if validation shows the product needs rethinking?

acceptedAnswer.text: That is the point of validating before building. Discovering a flawed assumption during design costs a design revision. Discovering the same flaw once development is underway costs a rebuild. Where a finding materially changes the commercial case, we report it directly — we are paid for the work, not for the answer you were hoping for.

mainEntity.name: Where does AI fit into the product design?

acceptedAnswer.text: Where AI creates genuine commercial value, we design it into the product architecture from the start — with the governance, data handling and cost model defined up front. We do not bolt AI onto a finished product, because retrofitting it usually means rebuilding the data model underneath it.

mainEntity.name: How much of our time does this take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A few hours a week from you or a nominated decision-maker, in facilitated working sessions plus review of the artefacts produced between them. You bring domain expertise, industry knowledge and the authority to make prioritisation calls. We bring the product framework and do the production work. This requires your judgement, not your labour.

mainEntity.name: Who owns the design files and the prototype?

acceptedAnswer.text: You do, on completion. Every document, wireframe, design file, prototype and asset transfers to you, including native editable Figma files. No licence conditions, no hostage terms, and no requirement to build with us.

mainEntity.name: How is the engagement priced?

You get a fixed price for a fixed scope, confirmed in writing before you commit — not a rate card, and not an hourly rate that turns into a blank cheque. No additional charges arise to complete the agreed scope. Book a fit call and we will scope it and quote it.

mainEntity.name: Do we need the Commercial Opportunity Assessment first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. If the commercial case is already proven — you know who pays, what they pay, and that the numbers work — you can start here. If it is not, the Commercial Opportunity Assessment tests that first, and designing a product whose business model has never been examined is how expensive rework begins.

mainEntity.name: What does it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Foundation is a fixed one-off investment. The Engine runs on a fixed monthly investment. We confirm both on your discovery call — not because we're being cagey, but because the right scope depends on your stage, your market, and how much of your go-to-market you want us to run. You'll leave that call with exact numbers.

mainEntity.name: Why is Foundation mandatory?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because running campaigns before the system exists is how agencies burn your money and call it testing. Foundation builds the asset. The retainer runs it. Skipping the first makes the second worthless.

mainEntity.name: Why is the retainer month-to-month if you want us long-term?

acceptedAnswer.text: Lock-in is what agencies use when the work doesn't hold clients on its own. We'd rather earn it. Foundation is paid upfront because it's a defined build with a defined output — after that, you decide every month.

mainEntity.name: How do you measure results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every campaign launches with a defined metric attached to it — the thing that campaign is meant to move. We report against those metrics monthly, alongside attributed pipeline value so you can see dollars progressing through the funnel. We'll be straight with you that B2B attribution is directional rather than exact. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you a spreadsheet.

mainEntity.name: Do we own what you build?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your CRM instance, your data, your content, your campaigns, your automations — yours, on full payment, including if the engagement ends. We retain our own frameworks, templates and internal tooling.

mainEntity.name: What happens if we want to pause or stop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Thirty days' written notice. We hand over your instance, your assets, and your documentation. No exit fee, no hostage situation.

mainEntity.name: Can you take on our second business?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — once the first one's working. We won't pitch you an expansion before we've earned it. Subsequent businesses get Foundation at a reduced rate because we already know how you operate.

mainEntity.name: How much of this is done by AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enough to make the price possible. Not enough to make the quality suffer. Every deliverable passes a human quality gate, and every strategic decision is made by a person you can name and call.

mainEntity.name: How will we know where things stand?

acceptedAnswer.text: You will always know. Once we finalise a campaign, your GTM Lead walks you through the plan and keeps you updated on progress and deliverables as they land. Nothing sits in a black box, and you will never have to chase an update.

mainEntity.name: What happens if you think we shouldn't proceed?

You are paying for the judgement, not for agreement — and a straight answer you didn't want is worth considerably more than a comfortable one that costs you two years.
